"Rocket", "Meteor", "Sunrise" - the legendary hydrofoil vessels, their past and present.

These brainchilds of the genius designer Rostislav Alekseev, who once plowed rivers and shallow waters around the world, are now experiencing hard times. Most of them went to scrap metal back in Soviet times, the fate of some is rather exotic (for example, a village shop in Krasnoyarsk or a sports cafe in the Chelyabinsk region), and some of them are all at nothing and they continue to serve people in our time. A little more about this:

  • "Meteor-196" It was built in 1984, it is not operated since 1994, now it is on the Zaozerskaya repair and maintenance base of the fleet, Perm.

  • Rocket 69 in the Pereboro microdistrict of Rybinsk, Yaroslavl Region. It was built in 1962, and now it's just a children's attraction in the park. Recently, in order to save the vessel, it was decided to restore the outer shell, in addition, the access of visitors inside, most likely, will be closed

  • Ladoga lake. Balaam. Meteor-191 "The Monk Seraphim". Flights between St. Petersburg and Valaam - this is one of the few lines on which the message by hydrofoil ships did not stop. All ships servicing this line have thematic names: for example, "Patriarch Alexy II", "Andrew Pervozvanny" or "Hegumen Nazari".

  • "Rocket" in the city of Moscow, the beginning of zero. Currently, only six "Raket" are running on-two in Finland as pleasure craft (one of them has underwater wings), two - the "Rocket-258" and the "Rocket-269" - still go on the voyage Routes in Yakutia. Another one is in Bratislava (the capital of Slovakia) and the city of Nefteyugansk.

  • The moored "Voskhod" in the delta of the Don River.

  • The moment of delivery of the "Rockets" in Kyshtym, November 1995

  • "Meteor" in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Most likely, in the frame Petro Express 01 - the only one of the three Ho Chi Minh Meteors, which is still on the move

  • In the north of Budapest, Hungary. year 2014. In Hungary, this type of vessel is called "S? Lyom" - "Falcon". S? Lyom II, who got into this frame, was launched in 1988.

  • "Meteor-001" in Nizhny Novgorod, near the plant "Krasnoe Sormovo", where ships of this type were designed. It was built in 1962, decommissioned in 1980, installed in 1982 as a monument, and in 2004 moved to a new location, about a kilometer from the previous one. On the pedestal it is written that the ship was built in 1959. The first "Meteor" was really built in 1959, but the fact is that on the pedestal is not the first, and the eighth in the ship - the first one was badly damaged after a collision with the barge, shortly after that it was cut for scrap in 1980. But now The "Meteor" that stands on the pedestal is really the first one that has survived.

  • And the oldest of the surviving "Rocket" (the seventh according to the bill, built in 1959) nowadays functions as a rural store in the village of Podtyosovo (Krasnoyarsk Territory).

  • A small digression from the topic: decommissioned ekranoplan on the dynamic air cushion "Volga-2", the Montenegrin shore of the Skadar Lake. Volga-2 is the first civilian-purpose ekranoplane designed in the Soviet Union and Russia, designed by Vitaly Dementiev. The Ekranoplan was produced at the Nizhny Novgorod aircraft factory "Sokol".

  • "Comet" and "Colchis" Tyrrhenian Sea, Neapolitan Bay of Naples, the port of Molo Beverello

  • Meteor-193 in Kazan, near the building of the River School. Built in 1984, decommissioned in 2004, installed as a monument in 2006.

Until 1979, shuttled between Kuibyshev (Samara) and Kazan, after which it was decommissioned and still stands in a park near the river station in Togliatti.
